--- title: cacheComponents description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js. related: links: - app/getting-started/caching - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote --- Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route. ## Usage To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file, together with [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching): ```ts filename="next.config.ts" import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } export default nextConfig ``` Set `partialPrefetching` explicitly. Leaving it unset logs a warning, because the first release of Cache Components did not include Partial Prefetching. Set it to `false` only while [migrating an app that adopted Cache Components before Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed. > **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge). When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations: - The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) - The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache` - The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) > **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components). Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed. Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together. > **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating. ## Navigation with Activity When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation. Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means: - Component state is preserved when navigating between routes - When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact - Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes. > **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth. Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing. ## Version History | Version | Change | | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | 16.0.0 | `cacheComponents` stabilized and moved from `experimental.cacheComponents` to the top-level `cacheComponents` option. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. | --- title: partialPrefetching description: Configure the default link prefetch behavior to fetch only the static parts of each route. related: title: Related description: View related API references and guides. links: - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch - app/api-reference/components/link - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching --- `partialPrefetching` enables Partial Prefetching at the app level. The framework prefetches the static parts of each route by default; set `prefetch={true}` on individual links to use [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) and fetch more. ## Usage ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} switcher import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } export default nextConfig ``` ```js filename="next.config.js" highlight={3} switcher module.exports = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } ``` `partialPrefetching` requires [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents). Without it, `next dev` and `next build` throw at config validation. ## Reference | Value | Description | | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `true` | Enables Partial Prefetching across the app. | | `false` | Keeps the previous prefetch behavior, for apps that adopted Cache Components before Partial Prefetching was available. | Leaving the option unset behaves like `false` and logs a warning when `cacheComponents` is enabled. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed. ## How prefetches resolve Before Partial Prefetching, Next.js prefetched per visible link: a page with N links to N routes produced ~N route prefetches as those links entered the viewport. With `partialPrefetching: true`, Next.js prefetches one reusable [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route instead. The App Shell contains rendered output that does not depend on a link's URL. URL-specific content, including content that depends on `params` or `searchParams`, resolves after navigation by default. App Shells are cached on the client, so links to the same route reuse one prefetch. The pattern is similar to per-route code splitting in single-page apps: one artifact per route, shared by every link that points to it. > **Good to know**: Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce an App Shell that includes session data. The framework auto-detects this and caches the shell per session on the client. A link can ask for more than the App Shell with [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch also resolves URL data like `params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL, and the cached content behind it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching). > **Good to know**: If you use `` to a route that hasn't opted into Partial Prefetching, a dev console error suggests enabling `partialPrefetching` app-wide or `prefetch = 'partial'` on the segment. The [dev warning Insight](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) covers each fix in detail. ## Per-segment overrides A segment that exports an explicit [`prefetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) value overrides the app-level default for that route. ## Version History | Version | Change | | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | 16.3.0 | `partialPrefetching` introduced. Requires `cacheComponents` to be enabled. | --- title: Dynamic Route Segments nav_title: Dynamic Segments description: Use Dynamic Segments to read URL path params and generate routes from dynamic data. related: title: Next Steps description: For more information on what to do next, we recommend the following sections links: - app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params --- A URL path is a sequence of path segments. In the App Router, a segment may be **static** (a literal value matched exactly) or **dynamic** (a placeholder that captures a value from the URL). When you don't know a segment's value ahead of time, define a Dynamic Segment to create routes from dynamic data. Next.js passes the captured values to your page via the path `params` prop, either filled in at request time or prerendered at build time. > **Good to know**: Dynamic Segments are often referred to as path params, route params, or URL params. ## Convention A Dynamic Segment can be created by wrapping a folder's name in square brackets: `[folderName]`. For example, a blog could include the following route `app/blog/[slug]/page.js` where `[slug]` is the Dynamic Segment for blog posts. ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher export default async function Page({ params, }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { const { slug } = await params return

"""Supabase access for the job queue: runs, steps, frictions and screenshots.

Needs SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY in the environment (worker/.env).
"""

import os
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from supabase import AsyncClient, acreate_client

BUCKET = "screenshots"

_client: AsyncClient | None = None


async def client() -> AsyncClient:
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        _client = await acreate_client(os.environ["SUPABASE_URL"], os.environ["SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY"])
    return _client


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


async def enqueue_run(url: str, goal: str, source: str = "live") -> dict:
    response = await (await client()).table("runs").insert(
        {"url": url, "goal": goal, "source": source}
    ).execute()
    return response.data[0]


async def claim_run() -> dict | None:
    """Take the oldest queued run and mark it running, or return None if the queue is empty."""
    response = await (await client()).rpc("claim_run").execute()
    return response.data[0] if response.data else None


async def add_step(
    run_id: str,
    idx: int,
    tool: str,
    thought: str,
    input: dict,
    result: dict,
    url: str | None,
    screenshot_path: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    await (await client()).table("steps").insert({
        "run_id": run_id,
        "idx": idx,
        "tool": tool,
        "thought": thought,
        "input": input,
        "result": result,
        "url": url,
        "screenshot_path": screenshot_path,
    }).execute()


async def add_friction(
    run_id: str,
    step_idx: int | None,
    kind: str,
    severity: str | None,
    expected: str,
    happened: str,
) -> None:
    await (await client()).table("frictions").insert({
        "run_id": run_id,
        "step_idx": step_idx,
        "kind": kind,
        "severity": severity,
        "expected": expected,
        "happened": happened,
    }).execute()


async def finish_run(run_id: str, result: dict, agent_version: str, brain_model: str) -> None:
    await (await client()).table("runs").update({
        "status": "done",
        "outcome": result.get("outcome"),
        "reason": result.get("reason"),
        "result": result,
        "cost_usd": result.get("usage", {}).get("estimated_cost_usd", {}).get("total"),
        "agent_version": agent_version,
        "brain_model": brain_model,
        "finished_at": _now(),
    }).eq("id", run_id).execute()


async def fail_run(
    run_id: str,
    error: str,
    agent_version: str | None = None,
    brain_model: str | None = None,

+-- Web app (added for web/). Safe to re-run.
+-- Who queued a run, as a keyed hash of their IP address (never the IP itself),
+-- for the per-visitor rate limit. Null for runs queued from the command line.
+alter table public.runs add column if not exists ip_hash text;
+  on public.runs (ip_hash, created_at) where ip_hash is not null;
+-- Queue a run from the web app, enforcing both limits in one transaction.
+-- The advisory lock serialises web enqueues, so two requests cannot both pass
+-- a limit and then both insert. Returns {"id": ...} or {"error": ...}.
+  select count(*) into queued_count from public.runs where status = 'queued';
+  select count(*), min(created_at) into recent_count, oldest_recent
+  where ip_hash = p_ip_hash and created_at > now() - interval '1 hour';
+  insert into public.runs (url, goal, source, ip_hash)
+revoke execute on function public.enqueue_web_run(text, text, text, integer, integer) from public, anon, authenticated;

"""Screenshot pages at a phone viewport over the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

Usage: python cdp_shot.py OUT_DIR WIDTH name=url [name=url ...]
Prints console errors and the first part of each page's visible text.
"""
import asyncio, base64, json, subprocess, sys, time, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

import websockets

CHROME = r"C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"
PORT = 9333


async def main(out_dir: Path, width: int, targets: list[str]) -> None:
    proc = subprocess.Popen([
        CHROME, "--headless=new", f"--remote-debugging-port={PORT}", "--disable-gpu", "--hide-scrollbars",
        f"--user-data-dir={out_dir / 'cdp-profile'}", "about:blank",
    ], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    try:
        for _ in range(50):
            try:
                pages = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/json"))
                break
            except OSError:
                time.sleep(0.2)
        ws_url = next(p["webSocketDebuggerUrl"] for p in pages if p["type"] == "page")
        async with websockets.connect(ws_url, max_size=50_000_000) as ws:
            counter = 0
            events: list[dict] = []

            async def call(method, **params):
                nonlocal counter
                counter += 1
                my_id = counter
                await ws.send(json.dumps({"id": my_id, "method": method, "params": params}))
                while True:
                    msg = json.loads(await ws.recv())
                    if msg.get("id") == my_id:
                        if "error" in msg:
                            raise RuntimeError(msg["error"])
                        return msg.get("result", {})
                    events.append(msg)

            await call("Page.enable")
            await call("Runtime.enable")
            await call("Log.enable")
            await call("Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride", width=width, height=844,
                       deviceScaleFactor=1, mobile=width < 600)
            for target in targets:
                name, url = target.split("=", 1)
                events.clear()
                await call("Page.navigate", url=url)
                await asyncio.sleep(5)
                await call("Runtime.evaluate", expression="1")  # drain pending events
                height = (await call("Runtime.evaluate", returnByValue=True,
                                     expression="document.documentElement.scrollHeight"))["result"]["value"]
                scroll_w = (await call("Runtime.evaluate", returnByValue=True,
                                       expression="document.documentElement.scrollWidth"))["result"]["value"]
                text = (await call("Runtime.evaluate", returnByValue=True,
                                   expression="document.body.innerText"))["result"]["value"]
                shot = await call("Page.captureScreenshot", format="png", captureBeyondViewport=True,
                                  clip={"x": 0, "y": 0, "width": width, "height": min(height, 6000), "scale": 1})
                (out_dir / f"{name}.png").write_bytes(base64.b64decode(shot["data"]))
                errors = [
                    e["params"].get("entry", e["params"]).get("text") or json.dumps(e["params"])[:300]
                    for e in events
                    if e.get("method") in ("Log.entryAdded", "Runtime.exceptionThrown")
                    or (e.get("method") == "Runtime.consoleAPICalled" and e["params"].get("type") == "error")
                ]
                print(f"== {name}: height {height}, scrollWidth {scroll_w} (viewport {width})")
                for err in errors:

"""Screenshot pages at a phone viewport over the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

Usage: python cdp_shot.py OUT_DIR WIDTH name=url [name=url ...]
Prints console errors and the first part of each page's visible text.
"""
import asyncio, base64, json, subprocess, sys, time, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

import websockets

CHROME = r"C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"
PORT = 9333


async def main(out_dir: Path, width: int, targets: list[str]) -> None:
    proc = subprocess.Popen([
        CHROME, "--headless=new", f"--remote-debugging-port={PORT}", "--disable-gpu", "--hide-scrollbars",
        f"--user-data-dir={out_dir / 'cdp-profile'}", "about:blank",
    ], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    try:
        for _ in range(50):
            try:
                pages = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/json"))
                break
            except OSError:
                time.sleep(0.2)
        ws_url = next(p["webSocketDebuggerUrl"] for p in pages if p["type"] == "page")
        async with websockets.connect(ws_url, max_size=50_000_000) as ws:
            counter = 0
            events: list[dict] = []

            async def call(method, **params):
                nonlocal counter
                counter += 1
                my_id = counter
                await ws.send(json.dumps({"id": my_id, "method": method, "params": params}))
                while True:
                    msg = json.loads(await ws.recv())
                    if msg.get("id") == my_id:
                        if "error" in msg:
                            raise RuntimeError(msg["error"])
                        return msg.get("result", {})
                    events.append(msg)

            await call("Page.enable")
            await call("Runtime.enable")
            await call("Log.enable")
            await call("Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride", width=width, height=844,
                       deviceScaleFactor=1, mobile=width < 600)
            for target in targets:
                name, url = target.split("=", 1)
                events.clear()
                await call("Page.navigate", url=url)
                await asyncio.sleep(5)
                await call("Runtime.evaluate", expression="1")  # drain pending events
                height = (await call("Runtime.evaluate", returnByValue=True,
                                     expression="document.documentElement.scrollHeight"))["result"]["value"]
                scroll_w = (await call("Runtime.evaluate", returnByValue=True,
                                       expression="document.documentElement.scrollWidth"))["result"]["value"]
                text = (await call("Runtime.evaluate", returnByValue=True,
                                   expression="document.body.innerText"))["result"]["value"]
                shot = await call("Page.captureScreenshot", format="png", captureBeyondViewport=True,
                                  clip={"x": 0, "y": 0, "width": width, "height": min(height, 6000), "scale": 1})
                (out_dir / f"{name}.png").write_bytes(base64.b64decode(shot["data"]))
                errors = [
                    e["params"].get("entry", e["params"]).get("text") or json.dumps(e["params"])[:300]
                    for e in events
                    if e.get("method") in ("Log.entryAdded", "Runtime.exceptionThrown")
                    or (e.get("method") == "Runtime.consoleAPICalled" and e["params"].get("type") == "error")
                ]
                print(f"== {name}: height {height}, scrollWidth {scroll_w} (viewport {width})")
                for err in errors:
                    print("   console:", str(err)[:300])
                print("   text:", " | ".join(line for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip())[:500])
    finally:
        proc.terminate()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main(Path(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3:]))

content.text:
The web app is built and passes typecheck, lint and `next build`. Nothing has touched your real Supabase yet: I tested against a fake Supabase I ran locally, and the new SQL has not been run anywhere.

**What I tested:**
- **URL checks:** I sent real requests to the running app. All of these were rejected with a plain message:
  - ftp addresses
  - localhost
  - addresses with a port (`:8080`, `:3000`)
  - 192.168.x.x
  - the cloud metadata IP 169.254.169.254
  - `::ffff:127.0.0.1` and `2130706433` (both are 127.0.0.1)
  - URLs with a username and password
  - single-word hosts
  - a domain that doesn't exist
  - `localtest.me`, a public name that resolves to 127.0.0.1
- **Other API errors:** missing permission box, a goal over 500 characters, a bad request body, and an unknown run id (404).
- **Full flow against the fake:** a normal submit returns the new run's id; a full queue returns 503; the hourly limit returns 429 with Retry-After; an unknown run returns 404.
- **Run page at 390 px (phone width), in Chrome:** I loaded every state: queued, running, done, failed and not found.
  - The running page picked up new steps every 2 seconds and stopped polling when the run finished.
  - Nothing scrolls sideways.
  - The report looked right in a screenshot; I tidied the wording on the agent-issue card after looking at it.
- **Key safety:** the browser bundle contains no key, no Supabase client code and no env variable names.

**Not tested:**
- The SQL itself.
- A real run going from the web app to the worker and back.
- The landing form's inline error messages in a browser (I tested the API behind them).
- Light mode: my screenshots rendered in dark mode.

**Choices you should know about:**
- **Queue limit:** a new run is rejected once 20 are already queued, so the queue never holds more than 20.
- **No race between limits:** one SQL function, `enqueue_web_run`, checks both limits and inserts the run in a single transaction, so two requests can't both slip past a limit.
- **Hashed IP:** the hash is keyed with the service role key unless you set `IP_HASH_SECRET`. The raw IP is never stored.
- **The rate limit isn't strong:** it trusts the `X-Forwarded-For` header, which is only safe behind a proxy that sets it (Vercel does). Locally anyone can fake it.
- **URL checks can be bypassed:** I check DNS when the form is submitted, but the worker's browser looks the name up again later and can follow redirects. A determined attacker could still reach a private address. Closing that properly means blocking private IPs inside the worker's browser.
- **Failed runs hide the reason:** the API returns a null reason for failed runs, because it's an internal error message. The page says "this tells you nothing about your site".
- **Report pages are marked noindex**, so search engines won't list them.
- **Packages:** I pinned `@supabase/supabase-js` to 2.117.2, the newest release that's at least two weeks old, plus `server-only`, which makes the build fail if the Supabase helper is ever imported into browser code. `npm install` reported audit warnings that I didn't investigate.

## What SQL to run

In the Supabase dashboard, open **SQL Editor → New query**, paste the whole of `supabase/schema.sql`, and click **Run**. It's safe to re-run, so it doesn't matter whether you already ran the earlier version. The new part is at the bottom: it adds an `ip_hash` column, an index on it, and the `enqueue_web_run` function, which only the service role can call.

To check it worked:
```sql
select column_name from information_schema.columns where table_name = 'runs' and column_name = 'ip_hash';  -- 1 row
select proname from pg_proc where proname = 'enqueue_web_run';                                              -- 1 row
```

## How to run it locally

1. **`web/.env.local`:** add the same two values you put in `worker/.env`:
   ```
   SUPABASE_URL=https://<your-project-ref>.supabase.co
   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<service_role key>
   ```
   You can also add `IP_HASH_SECRET=<any long random string>`, which is optional. Never add a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` copy of the key.
2. **Terminal 1, the web app:**
   ```
   cd web
   npm install
   npm run dev
   ```
   Then open http://localhost:3000.
3. **Terminal 2, the worker:** from `worker/`, run `.venv\Scripts\python.exe main.py`. Without it, runs stay "Waiting for a free browser".
4. **Try it:** submit `https://www.saucedemo.com` with the permission box ticked. You'll land on `/run/<id>` and watch the steps arrive. You can't test your own `localhost` app this way, because the URL checks reject it.

New files are `web/lib/`, `web/app/api/runs/route.ts`, `web/app/api/runs/[id]/route.ts`, `web/app/run-form.tsx` and `web/app/run/[id]/`. I also changed `layout.tsx`, `page.tsx`, `globals.css`, `package.json` and `schema.sql`. Nothing is committed. If you want it, I can also add this session to `hackathon.md`.

An automated security review flagged the same gap I mentioned in my last message: the app checks the address only once, when the form is submitted.

- **The risk:** later, the worker's browser looks the site up again and follows redirects. A site could then send it to a private address, such as localhost or the cloud metadata service. On your laptop, that means your own machine and home network.
- **The fix:** block private addresses where the browser actually connects. The worker would check every request and navigation and reject private ones, or the worker would run behind a network proxy or firewall that blocks them. Either covers redirects.
- **When it matters:** before the web app is open to strangers. For local testing with sites you choose, the current check is enough.

I haven't changed anything, because the fix belongs in `worker/` and is outside what you asked for here. Want me to add the per-request blocking to the worker next?

    try:

    finally:

local_browser = LocalBrowser()
browserbase = BrowserbaseBrowser()


async def _launch_local_browser(options: _LocalBrowserOptions) -> ResolvedBrowserSource:
    _validate_local_browser_options(options)
    chrome_path = _find_chrome_path(options.executable_path)
    port = _resolve_chrome_port(options.port)
    profile = _resolve_chrome_profile(options)
    flags = _local_browser_flags(
        options,
        port=port,
        user_data_dir=profile.path,
        disable_sandbox=_should_disable_chromium_sandbox(options),
    )
    process: _ChromeProcess | None = None
    try:
        try:
            launched_process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
                chrome_path,
                *flags,
                stdin=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
                start_new_session=sys.platform != "win32",
            )
            process = launched_process
        except OSError as error:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to start Chrome: {error}") from error
        await _wait_for_chrome(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}", launched_process)
    except BaseException as launch_error:
        try:
            if process is not None:
                await _close_local_chrome(process, profile)
            elif profile.remove:
                await _remove_chrome_profile(profile.path)
        except BaseException as cleanup_error:
            raise _combined_error(
                "Chrome launch failed and browser cleanup also failed",
                [launch_error, cleanup_error],
            ) from launch_error
        raise

    async def close() -> None:
        await _close_local_chrome(launched_process, profile)

    return ResolvedBrowserSource(
        cdp_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}",
        keep_alive=options.keep_alive or False,
        _close_callback=close,
    )


def _validate_local_browser_options(options: _LocalBrowserOptions) -> None:
    if options.viewport is not None and (
        options.viewport.width <= 0 or options.viewport.height <= 0
    ):
        raise ValueError("Chrome viewport dimensions must be positive integers")
    if options.device_scale_factor is not None and (
        not math.isfinite(options.device_scale_factor) or options.device_scale_factor <= 0
    ):
        raise ValueError("Chrome device scale factor must be positive and finite")
    if options.proxy is not None:
        if not options.proxy.server:
            raise ValueError("Chrome proxy server is required")
        if options.proxy.username is not None or options.proxy.password is not None:
            raise NotImplementedError("Authenticated local browser proxies are not implemented yet")


def _resolve_chrome_profile(options: _LocalBrowserOptions) -> _ChromeProfile:
    if options.user_data_dir not in (None, ""):
        path = Path(options.user_data_dir)
        path.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        return _ChromeProfile(path=path, remove=False)
    path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="stagehand-chrome-"))
    return _ChromeProfile(path=path, remove=options.preserve_user_data_dir is not True)


async def _wait_for_chrome(
    cdp_url: str,
    process: _WaitableChromeProcess,
) -> None:
    exited = asyncio.create_task(process.wait())
    ready: asyncio.Task[bool] | None = None
    delay: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
    try:
        while True:
            if process.returncode is not None:
                raise _chrome_exited_before_ready_error(process.returncode)

            ready = asyncio.create_task(_chrome_debugging_ready(cdp_url))
            done, _ = await asyncio.wait((ready, exited), return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
            if exited in done:
                ready.cancel()
                with suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                    await ready
                raise _chrome_exited_before_ready_error(exited.result())
            if ready.result():
                if process.returncode is not None or exited.done():
                    raise _chrome_exited_before_ready_error(process.returncode)
                return

            delay = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.sleep(_CHROME_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS))
            done, _ = await asyncio.wait((delay, exited), return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
            if exited in done:
                delay.cancel()

async def _launch_local_browser(options: _LocalBrowserOptions) -> ResolvedBrowserSource:
    _validate_local_browser_options(options)
    chrome_path = _find_chrome_path(options.executable_path)
    port = _resolve_chrome_port(options.port)
    profile = _resolve_chrome_profile(options)
    flags = _local_browser_flags(
        options,
        port=port,
        user_data_dir=profile.path,
        disable_sandbox=_should_disable_chromium_sandbox(options),
    )
    process: _ChromeProcess | None = None
    try:
        try:
            launched_process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
                chrome_path,
                *flags,
                stdin=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
                start_new_session=sys.platform != "win32",
            )
            process = launched_process
        except OSError as error:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to start Chrome: {error}") from error
        await _wait_for_chrome(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}", launched_process)
    except BaseException as launch_error:
        try:
            if process is not None:
                await _close_local_chrome(process, profile)
            elif profile.remove:
                await _remove_chrome_profile(profile.path)
        except BaseException as cleanup_error:
            raise _combined_error(
                "Chrome launch failed and browser cleanup also failed",
                [launch_error, cleanup_error],
            ) from launch_error
        raise

    async def close() -> None:
        await _close_local_chrome(launched_process, profile)

    return ResolvedBrowserSource(
        cdp_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}",
        keep_alive=options.keep_alive or False,
        _close_callback=close,
    )


def _validate_local_browser_options(options: _LocalBrowserOptions) -> None:
    if options.viewport is not None and (
        options.viewport.width <= 0 or options.viewport.height <= 0
    ):
        raise ValueError("Chrome viewport dimensions must be positive integers")
    if options.device_scale_factor is not None and (
        not math.isfinite(options.device_scale_factor) or options.device_scale_factor <= 0
    ):
        raise ValueError("Chrome device scale factor must be positive and finite")
    if options.proxy is not None:
        if not options.proxy.server:
            raise ValueError("Chrome proxy server is required")
        if options.proxy.username is not None or options.proxy.password is not None:
            raise NotImplementedError("Authenticated local browser proxies are not implemented yet")


def _resolve_chrome_profile(options: _LocalBrowserOptions) -> _ChromeProfile:
    if options.user_data_dir not in (None, ""):
        path = Path(options.user_data_dir)
        path.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        return _ChromeProfile(path=path, remove=False)
    path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="stagehand-chrome-"))
    return _ChromeProfile(path=path, remove=options.preserve_user_data_dir is not True)


async def _wait_for_chrome(
    cdp_url: str,
    process: _WaitableChromeProcess,
) -> None:
    exited = asyncio.create_task(process.wait())
    ready: asyncio.Task[bool] | None = None
    delay: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
    try:
        while True:
            if process.returncode is not None:
                raise _chrome_exited_before_ready_error(process.returncode)

            ready = asyncio.create_task(_chrome_debugging_ready(cdp_url))
            done, _ = await asyncio.wait((ready, exited), return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
            if exited in done:
                ready.cancel()
                with suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                    await ready
                raise _chrome_exited_before_ready_error(exited.result())
            if ready.result():
                if process.returncode is not None or exited.done():
                    raise _chrome_exited_before_ready_error(process.returncode)
                return

            delay = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.sleep(_CHROME_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS))
            done, _ = await asyncio.wait((delay, exited), return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
            if exited in done:
                delay.cancel()
                with suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                    await delay
                raise _chrome_exited_before_ready_error(exited.result())
    finally:
        for pending in (ready, delay):
            if pending is not None and not pending.done():
                pending.cancel()
                with suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                    await pending
        if not exited.done():
            exited.cancel()
            with suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await exited

def _local_browser_flags(
    options: _LocalBrowserOptions,
    *,
    port: int,
    user_data_dir: Path,
    disable_sandbox: bool,
) -> list[str]:
    ignored_default_args = options.ignore_default_args
    ignored_flags = set(ignored_default_args) if isinstance(ignored_default_args, list) else set()
    include_defaults = ignored_default_args is not True
    viewport = (
        options.viewport if options.viewport is not None else LocalViewport(width=1280, height=800)
    )
    window_size_flag = f"--window-size={viewport.width},{viewport.height}"

    return [
        *(
            [flag for flag in _DEFAULT_CHROME_FLAGS if flag not in ignored_flags]
            if include_defaults
            else []
        ),
        *(
            [window_size_flag]
            if options.viewport is not None
            or (include_defaults and window_size_flag not in ignored_flags)
            else []
        ),
        f"--remote-debugging-port={port}",
        f"--user-data-dir={user_data_dir}",
        *(["--headless"] if options.headless is True else []),
        *(["--auto-open-devtools-for-tabs"] if options.devtools is True else []),
        *(["--no-sandbox"] if disable_sandbox else []),
        *([f"--proxy-server={options.proxy.server}"] if options.proxy else []),
        *(
            [f"--proxy-bypass-list={options.proxy.bypass}"]
            if options.proxy and options.proxy.bypass
            else []
        ),
        *([f"--lang={options.locale}"] if options.locale else []),
        *(
            [f"--force-device-scale-factor={options.device_scale_factor}"]
            if options.device_scale_factor is not None
            else []
        ),
        *(["--touch-events=enabled"] if options.has_touch is True else []),
        *(["--ignore-certificate-errors"] if options.ignore_https_errors is True else []),
        *(options.args or []),
        "about:blank",
    ]

import os

from stagehand import Stagehand, local_browser

from config import DEVICE_SCALE_FACTOR, LOOKUP_MODEL
from egress import CHROME_EXTRA_ARGS, CHROME_PROXY_BYPASS, EgressGuard


async def open_browser():
    """Start the egress guard, launch a local Chrome window behind it and attach Stagehand.

    Every request Chrome makes goes through the guard, which refuses private,
    loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses (see egress.py).
    """
    guard = EgressGuard()
    await guard.start()
    try:
        browser = await local_browser.launch(
            headless=False,
            device_scale_factor=DEVICE_SCALE_FACTOR,
            proxy_server=guard.proxy_server,
            proxy_bypass=CHROME_PROXY_BYPASS,
            args=CHROME_EXTRA_ARGS,
        )
    except BaseException:
        await guard.close()
        raise
    try:
        stagehand = await Stagehand.create(
            browser=browser,
            model=LOOKUP_MODEL,
            model_api_key=os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"],
        )
    except BaseException:
        try:
            await browser.close()
        finally:
            await guard.close()
        raise
    page = (await browser.context.pages())[0]
    return browser, stagehand, page, guard


async def close_browser(browser, stagehand, guard):
    """Close Stagehand before the browser, as the Stagehand docs require, then the guard."""
    try:
        await stagehand.close()
    finally:
        try:
            await browser.close()
        finally:
            await guard.close()

import ipaddress

from dotenv import load_dotenv

import egress  # noqa: E402

TEST_ORIGIN = ipaddress.ip_address("127.0.0.1")

    """A tiny HTTP server that counts requests and answers with a fixed response."""

    async def __aenter__(self):
        async def handle(reader, writer):
            await reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")
            self.hits += 1
            writer.write(self.response)
            await writer.drain()
            writer.close()

        self.server = await asyncio.start_server(handle, self.host, 0)
        self.port = self.server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
        self.server.close()
        await self.server.wait_closed()

    return (f"HTTP/1.1 {status}\r\n{headers}Content-Length: {len(body)}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{body}").encode()

    reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", guard.port)

    await writer.drain()
    status = (await reader.readline()).decode().strip()
    writer.close()
    return status

    def test_non_public_addresses_are_blocked(self):
        for address in ["127.0.0.1", "10.0.0.5", "172.16.3.4", "192.168.1.1", "169.254.169.254", "100.64.0.1",
                        "0.0.0.0", "::1", "fd00::1", "fe80::1", "::ffff:127.0.0.1", "64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe"]:

    async def test_redirect_to_private_address_is_refused_and_ends_run_as_blocked(self):
        from visit import first_visit

        async with Server("127.0.0.2", http_response("200 OK", body="secret")) as secret:

        self.assertEqual(result["outcome"], "blocked")
        self.assertIn("127.0.0.2", result["reason"])
        self.assertEqual(result["steps"], 0, "the run should end before any model call")

    unittest.main()

    async def _devtools_tunnel(self, reader, writer, host: str, port: int) -> None:
        """Forward a tunnel to Chrome's DevTools port only if its first request comes from an extension.

        Stagehand launches Chrome with --remote-allow-origins=*, so DevTools itself
        would accept a websocket from any page. A DevTools websocket is plain HTTP
        inside the tunnel, and browsers always send an Origin header that pages
        cannot forge, so the guard checks it here instead.
        """
        writer.write(b"HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established\r\n\r\n")
        await writer.drain()
        try:
            head = await asyncio.wait_for(reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n"), HEADER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
        except (asyncio.IncompleteReadError, asyncio.LimitOverrunError, asyncio.TimeoutError):
            return
        request_line, *header_lines = head.decode("latin-1").split("\r\n")
        origin = next(
            (line.split(":", 1)[1].strip() for line in header_lines if line.lower().startswith("origin:")), ""
        )
        task = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(
            _guarded_devtools_check(origin, request_line[:200]), context=self._context.copy()
        )
        if not (await task)["allowed"]:
            self.blocks.append({"host": host, "port": port, "url": f"DevTools: {request_line[:200]}",
                                "addresses": [host], "reason": f"DevTools request from origin {origin or 'none'}"})
            return
        upstream_reader, upstream = await _open_vetted(["127.0.0.1"], port)
        if upstream is None:
            return
        try:
            upstream.write(head)
            await asyncio.gather(_pipe(reader, upstream), _pipe(upstream_reader, writer))
        finally:
            upstream.close()

"""Tests for the egress guard.

Usage: python -m unittest test_egress -v

The redirect test opens a real Chrome window and goes through first_visit, but
stops before the first model call, so it costs nothing. It needs
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in worker/.env only because Stagehand.create requires one.
Test servers listen on loopback, so 127.0.0.1 is treated as public for the
test origin; the redirect target 127.0.0.2 stays private.
"""

import asyncio
import ipaddress
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv(Path(__file__).parent / ".env")

import egress  # noqa: E402

REAL_IS_BLOCKED = egress.is_blocked_address
TEST_ORIGIN = ipaddress.ip_address("127.0.0.1")


def origin_is_public(address):
    return False if address == TEST_ORIGIN else REAL_IS_BLOCKED(address)


class Server:
    """A tiny HTTP server that counts requests and answers with a fixed response."""

    def __init__(self, host: str, response: bytes):
        self.host, self.response, self.hits, self.port = host, response, 0, 0

    async def __aenter__(self):
        async def handle(reader, writer):
            await reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")
            self.hits += 1
            writer.write(self.response)
            await writer.drain()
            writer.close()

        self.server = await asyncio.start_server(handle, self.host, 0)
        self.port = self.server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
        self.server.close()
        await self.server.wait_closed()


def http_response(status: str, headers: str = "", body: str = "") -> bytes:
    return (f"HTTP/1.1 {status}\r\n{headers}Content-Length: {len(body)}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{body}").encode()


async def proxy_request(guard: egress.EgressGuard, request: str) -> str:
    reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", guard.port)
    writer.write(request.encode())
    await writer.drain()
    status = (await reader.readline()).decode().strip()
    writer.close()
    return status


class AddressRules(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_non_public_addresses_are_blocked(self):
        for address in ["127.0.0.1", "10.0.0.5", "172.16.3.4", "192.168.1.1", "169.254.169.254", "100.64.0.1",
                        "0.0.0.0", "::1", "fd00::1", "fe80::1", "::ffff:127.0.0.1", "64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe"]:
            with self.subTest(address=address):
                self.assertTrue(egress.is_blocked_address(ipaddress.ip_address(address)))

    def test_public_addresses_are_allowed(self):
        for address in ["8.8.8.8", "93.184.215.14", "2606:4700:4700::1111"]:
            with self.subTest(address=address):
                self.assertFalse(egress.is_blocked_address(ipaddress.ip_address(address)))


class ProxyRefusals(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_private_targets_are_refused_and_never_contacted(self):
        async with Server("127.0.0.2", http_response("200 OK", body="secret")) as secret:
            guard = egress.EgressGuard()
            await guard.start()
            try:
                plain = await proxy_request(
                    guard, f"GET http://127.0.0.2:{secret.port}/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.2\r\n\r\n")
                tunnel = await proxy_request(guard, "CONNECT localhost:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost:443\r\n\r\n")
                metadata = await proxy_request(
                    guard, "GET http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 169.254.169.254\r\n\r\n")
            finally:
                await guard.close()
        self.assertIn("403", plain)
        self.assertIn("403", tunnel)
        self.assertIn("403", metadata)
        self.assertEqual(secret.hits, 0)
        self.assertEqual([b["host"] for b in guard.blocks], ["127.0.0.2", "localhost", "169.254.169.254"])

    async def test_unresolvable_host_is_not_a_safety_block(self):
        guard = egress.EgressGuard()
        await guard.start()
        try:
            status = await proxy_request(
                guard, "GET http://no-such-host.invalid/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: no-such-host.invalid\r\n\r\n")
        finally:
            await guard.close()
        self.assertIn("502", status)
        self.assertEqual(guard.blocks, [])


class RedirectInRealBrowser(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_redirect_to_private_address_is_refused_and_ends_run_as_blocked(self):
        from visit import first_visit

        async with Server("127.0.0.2", http_response("200 OK", body="secret")) as secret:
            redirect = http_response("302 Found", f"Location: http://127.0.0.2:{secret.port}/secret\r\n")
            async with Server("127.0.0.1", redirect) as origin:
                with mock.patch("egress.is_blocked_address", origin_is_public):
                    result = await first_visit(
                        f"http://127.0.0.1:{origin.port}/", "Look around.", "test-egress-redirect")

        self.assertGreaterEqual(origin.hits, 1, "the allowed origin should have been reached through the proxy")
        self.assertEqual(secret.hits, 0, "the private redirect target must never be contacted")
        self.assertEqual(result["outcome"], "blocked")
        self.assertIn("127.0.0.2", result["reason"])
        self.assertEqual(result["steps"], 0, "the run should end before any model call")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# neatHack — First User

## Project

- **Name:** First User
- **Purpose:** An AI agent that uses a founder's web app like a first-time customer and reports where it got stuck.
- **Problem:** Pending.

## Team

- **Team name:** test
- **Members:** Divyanshu Verma (solo)

## Stack

- `worker/` — Python 3.11 worker; the only service that calls a model.
  - Anthropic Python SDK (`anthropic` 1.13.0). Brain model: `claude-sonnet-5-5` by default, `claude-haiku-5-5` with `BRAIN_MODEL=haiku`. `hello.py` uses `claude-opus-5-5`.
  - Stagehand Python SDK (`stagehand` 4.2.0) driving a local Chrome window, with `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` as its lookup model. That is the newest Haiku Stagehand 4.2.0 accepts.
  - neatlogs Python SDK (`neatlogs[anthropic]` 1.4.26), workflow `first-visit-test`
  - `pydantic` 2.14.0 for Stagehand extract schemas; `python-dotenv` for loading `worker/.env`
- `web/` — Next.js 16.4.0 / React 19.3.0 app (scaffold only so far; no model calls).
- Entire — checkpoints are on (`.entire/settings.json`, git-refs storage). Commits carry an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.
- GitHub — `origin` is https://github.com/devs-dv/first-user (visibility not confirmed).
- cfo.ai — pending (not set up yet).

## Build log

### 2026-10-10 — neatHack setup and neatlogs tracing

Completed:
- Saved the neatHack skill from https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/skill to `.claude/skills/neathack/SKILL.md`.
- Created this `hackathon.md`.
- Installed `neatlogs[anthropic]` (1.4.26) into `worker/.venv` with `pip install -U`, as the [Python SDK docs](https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/python) instruct.
- Added tracing to `worker/hello.py` only: `neatlogs.init()` with `workflow_name="first-visit-test"` and the key read from `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` in the environment, `neatlogs.wrap()` around the Anthropic client, and `neatlogs.flush()` plus `neatlogs.shutdown()` at the end. `load_dotenv()` runs before `init()`, as the docs require. No other behavior changed.

Tests that ran:
- `python -m neatlogs doctor --local --json` passed (`neatlogs.doctor/v2`, schema `2`, 4 spans captured, 0 dropped).
- `python worker/hello.py` exited 0. The model replied and the SDK shut down cleanly.

Not yet verified:
- Whether the trace appears in the neatlogs dashboard under `first-visit-test`.
- `python -m neatlogs doctor --probe --json` (authenticated probe) has not run.

### 2026-10-10 — First commit, Entire checkpoint, published rules checked

Completed:
- The builder committed and pushed the setup as `ab7458b` ("Add worker with neatlogs tracing, neathack skill and build log") to `origin/main`. The commit is dated 2026-10-10 13:48 IST, inside the hackathon window.
- `.gitignore` now ignores `*.egg-info/`, so the generated packaging metadata stays out of the repo.
- Read the published rules at https://neatlogs.com/hackathon and https://luma.com/s5blr882, and recorded the confirmed requirements under Submission below.

Evidence:
- Entire: commit `ab7458b` carries the trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: 01M4JE8CYXZ6X24DWSCN9SJM0C`. This is the first Entire evidence for the project.
- Secrets check: `git ls-files` lists no `.env` file. `worker/.env` is ignored by the root `.gitignore`.

Tests that ran:
- None this session. No code changed after `ab7458b`.

Still open from the previous entry:
- The neatlogs dashboard trace for `first-visit-test` is not yet confirmed, and `doctor --probe` has not run.

Decisions pending from the builder:
- The one-sentence problem statement for the Project section.
- Whether the GitHub repo is public. The rules require a public repository, and visibility could not be checked from this machine because the `gh` CLI is not installed.

### 2026-10-10 — Browsing agent v1 (committed as `ac3b598`)

Not logged at the time, so this entry is recorded afterwards.

Completed:
- Added `worker/config.py`, `browser.py`, `tools.py` (`look`, `do`, `scroll`, `go_back`, `note_friction`, `finish`), `browse.py` (a hand-written Messages API tool loop under an `AGENT` span) and `run_once.py` (a CLI under a `WORKFLOW` span). Each `do` saves a screenshot to `worker/runs/<run_id>/`, which is gitignored.
- The builder committed this as `ac3b598` (2026-10-10 14:50 IST) with the trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: 01M4JHT3GYPPTJFPFBYH9XCBX8`.

Tests that ran:
- Run `20261010-140746`: outcome `achieved` on saucedemo in 10 steps.
- Run `20261010-140943`: crashed at step 18 because the Anthropic account ran out of credits. Before that it looped, reporting "Add to cart" as successful while the cart stayed empty.

Fixes:
- One action per turn (`disable_parallel_tool_use`).
- API errors now end a run with `outcome: "error"` and a JSON result instead of a traceback.

### 2026-10-10 — Cost controls and reliable clicks

Completed (cost):
- Prompt caching uses an explicit breakpoint on the system prompt, which covers tools plus system, and automatic caching for the conversation tail. The goal moved from the system prompt into the first user message, so the cached prefix is identical across runs. Look-result stubbing edits only `messages`, after the system breakpoint, so the system and tools cache survives it.
- Per-turn `max_tokens` is 2048, effort is `low` (`BRAIN_EFFORT`), and `MAX_STEPS` defaults to 15.
- `look()` now makes one Stagehand `extract` call (summary plus up to 15 items), truncates the output, and gets the URL and title from the page API. When the page fingerprint is unchanged it returns "unchanged" with no model call.
- Stagehand token deltas from `metrics()` are recorded on each tool span as `stagehand.*` attributes. Model and Stagehand tokens, plus an estimated cost, are summed into the final result JSON (`worker/costs.py`).
- A `GUARDRAIL` span (`budget_check`) runs before every model call. It stops the run with `gave_up` / `budget` above `MAX_RUN_TOKENS` (400,000) or `MAX_RUN_COST_USD` ($0.30).
- `BRAIN_MODEL` takes a model id or the alias `sonnet` or `haiku`.

Completed (clicks):
- Root cause: Stagehand's coordinate-based clicks often had no effect on saucedemo. `act` chose the right button (confirmed from its returned selector), but the click did not register, while a DOM click event did. The display runs at 125% scaling (device pixel ratio 1.25). Chrome now launches at device scale factor 1 (`DEVICE_SCALE_FACTOR`); after that, `locator.click` worked, but `act` clicks still sometimes missed.
- `do()` now fingerprints the page (URL plus a hash of visible text and form values) before and after. If `act` reports success but nothing changed, the result is `no_effect`. It then works through a recovery ladder, with each rung in its own span:
  - (a) `act(instruction)`
  - (b) `observe` then `act(action)`
  - (c) the observed selector through the locator API: `locator.click`, then `send_click_event`

  The result reports the rung that worked. If every rung fails, the model is told plainly and the case is recorded as an `agent_issue`, not as site friction.

Tests that ran (`python measure_clicks.py`, no brain model; log in, then add one item to the cart, 5 fresh browsers):

| | End-to-end success | Steps that changed the page | Reported success, nothing changed | Stagehand tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before (plain `act`, scale 1.25) | 0/5 | 15/20 | 5 (every "Add to cart") | 40,786 |
| After (ladder, scale 1.0) | 5/5 | 20/20 | 0 | 53,139 |

After the change, "Add to cart" succeeded on rung (c) in all 5 attempts. Rung (a) failed every time even at scale 1.0, so the ladder, not the scale fix, is what made it reliable.

Brain comparison on the saucedemo goal (estimated cost uses list prices in `config.py`):

| Brain | Run | Outcome | Steps | Total tokens | Estimated cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-haiku-5-5` | `20261010-150417` | achieved | 8 | 36,914 | $0.0172 (model $0.0010, Stagehand $0.0162) |
| `claude-sonnet-5-5` | `20261010-150521` | achieved | 8 | 36,509 | $0.0345 (model $0.0181, Stagehand $0.0163) |

- Caching worked in both runs: about 2,100 tokens were cache reads from step 2, and each later turn wrote only about 130–220 new tokens.
- A guardrail check with `MAX_RUN_COST_USD=0.001` stopped the run with `gave_up` / `budget` after 1 step (total $0.0021). That run's first request read the 2,127-token prefix from the cache, which shows reuse across runs.

Not yet verified:
- Whether the `stagehand.*` and `do.rung` span attributes show up in the neatlogs dashboard. They are set through OpenTelemetry's current span, which the neatlogs SDK itself uses.
- The ladder's agent-issue path in a full agent run. In both brain runs every action worked on rung (a).

## Demo

- URL: pending
- Instructions: pending

## Known limitations and next steps

- The agent has been tested on one demo site (saucedemo) with one easy goal. Both brains found no friction there, so the friction report is untested on a site that has real problems.
- Stagehand lookups are about 94% of a Haiku-brain run's cost: Stagehand 4.2.0 does not accept Claude Haiku 5.5, so lookups run on Haiku 4.5.
- With Sonnet at low effort, the `thought` field is often a fragment ("Open the cart.") rather than the first-person sentence the prompt asks for. Haiku followed the instruction.
- `web/` is an unmodified Next.js scaffold.
- Next steps (planned, not started):
  1. Confirm the `first-visit-test` traces and span attributes in the neatlogs dashboard, and run `doctor --probe`.
  2. Run the agent on a site with real friction to test the friction report and the agent-issue path.
  3. Try routing Stagehand's lookups through a cheaper model (Stagehand accepts an LLM callback in place of a model name).
  4. Sign up at cfo.ai/neathacks and draft the business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway). Per-run cost numbers are now available from the result JSON.
  5. Share progress publicly with #neatHack and keep the links here.

## Submission

Confirmed from https://neatlogs.com/hackathon (read 2026-10-10):
- **Window:** submissions open Monday, 12 October 2026, 7:00 PM IST and close at 11:55 PM IST. Winners are announced 16 October.

- **Evidence judges expect:** a before-and-after pair of traces with the compared numbers, neatlogs trace links or screenshots, Entire checkpoints or entire-graph output, a cfo.ai business plan, a run showing recovery from a failed action, #neatHack public posts, and a public repo with commits dated during the hackathon.

- Entire: checkpoints on `ab7458b` and `ac3b598`. This session's work is uncommitted.
- cfo.ai: pending (not signed up).
- Business plan: pending. Measured cost per saucedemo run is about $0.017 (Haiku brain) and $0.034 (Sonnet brain).
- Failure-recovery run: the recovery ladder recovered "Add to cart" in 5 of 5 measurement attempts. A full agent run that shows recovery is still pending.
- Building in public: pending (no posts recorded).
- Public repo: `origin` exists; visibility unconfirmed.
- Demo video: pending.

- Whether the `egress_check` and `devtools_check` spans nest under the run in the neatlogs dashboard. The guard copies the run's context when it starts so they should.

content.text:
The worker now refuses any browser request or navigation to private, loopback, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses, including after redirects. When that happens the run ends as `blocked`. All 6 tests in `worker/test_egress.py` pass, and a real saucedemo run through the guard reached the goal in 9 steps for $0.0292.

**How it works:**
- **One route out:** the worker starts a small filtering proxy (`worker/egress.py`) and launches Chrome so every request goes through it, including localhost. Chrome normally lets localhost skip a proxy; that exception is turned off. Redirects, images, scripts and websockets are all covered.
- **Check, then pin:** for each new host, the proxy looks up the name itself, refuses it if any address isn't public, and connects only to the address it checked. A site can't swap in a private address after the check.
- **neatlogs:** each check runs in a `GUARDRAIL` span named `egress_check`, once per host per run.
- **Ending the run:** the agent loop checks for a refusal before every model call and once after the loop. It ends the run as `blocked` with a reason like: "Stopped for safety: the site sent the browser to 127.0.0.2, which is a private, local or cloud-metadata address…". The web report shows it as "Got blocked" with that text.
- **Dead domains:** a host that doesn't exist (a dead analytics domain, say) is just refused. It doesn't end the run.

**Something you should know:** my first real run failed with "CDP websocket failed to open".
- **Cause:** Stagehand puts its own extension inside Chrome, and that extension connects to Chrome's local debugging port. The guard was refusing it.
- **Bigger issue:** Stagehand launches Chrome with a setting (`--remote-allow-origins=*`) that lets any page connect to that debugging port. A web page could have taken over the browser, and that was true before today's change too.
- **Fix:** the guard now lets connections reach that port only when they come from a browser extension. Pages can't fake this. The check runs in its own `GUARDRAIL` span (`devtools_check`). This closes both problems.

**The tests:**
- **Address rules:** blocked versus allowed addresses.
- **Private targets:** private IPs, `localhost` and the metadata IP all got 403 through the proxy, and the private test server received nothing.
- **Debugging port:** opens for an extension, refused for a page.
- **Dead domains:** refused without ending the run.
- **Redirect, in a real Chrome window, through `first_visit`:** a test site returned a redirect to 127.0.0.2. The server on 127.0.0.2 received 0 requests, and the run ended `blocked` with 0 steps, so there was no model cost. This is the test you asked for.
- **Control:** with Chrome's normal localhost exception left on, the same redirect test fails (the private server got 2 requests). So the test really depends on the guard.

**Trade-offs:**
- **Strict:** any refused request ends the run, including a stray third-party file on a private address, like a leftover `localhost` dev script. That's what you asked for.
- **One layer only:** the guard runs inside the worker process. A firewall on the worker machine would be a second layer, and none is set up.
- **Not seen yet:** I haven't confirmed in the neatlogs dashboard that the new spans appear under the run.

**`hackathon.md`:** I added entries for the web app session and this one. I also added a short entry for the job-queue session (`6a08b29`), which had no log entry, and marked it as written afterwards. I updated Stack, Known limitations and the Entire checkpoint list. The problem statement and whether the repo is public are still marked pending; you'll need to decide both.

I deleted an empty `package-lock.json` that one of my commands left at the repo root. Nothing is committed. The changes are in `worker/` (`egress.py` and `test_egress.py` are new; `browser.py`, `visit.py`, `browse.py`, `tools.py` and `measure_clicks.py` changed), the web app from last session, `supabase/schema.sql` and `hackathon.md`.

content.text:
Both fixes are in. I tested the wording fix on the run page; I couldn't reproduce the dev-overlay issue myself, so please check it on your side.

**1. The "1 Issue" on the run page.** It wasn't caused by our code.
- **Cause:** your dev server's log (`web/.next/dev/logs/next-development.log`) has a single error, a hydration mismatch. The only difference is a `cz-shortcut-listen="true"` attribute on `<body>`, which the ColorZilla browser extension adds to every page before React loads.
- **Fix:** I added `suppressHydrationWarning` to `<body>` in `web/app/layout.tsx`, with a comment explaining why. It ignores attribute differences on `<body>` only, so a real mismatch in our own pages would still be reported.
- **Check:** your server on port 3000 is still running and I left it alone, so I couldn't start a second dev server to reproduce this. Reload the run page in your browser and the overlay should be gone.

**2. Report wording.**
- **Retries:** a step that needed a retry now says so instead of "It worked."
  - **Second try:** "The first try had no effect. It worked on the second try, after our browser tool looked for the element again."
  - **Third try:** "The first two tries had no effect. It worked on the third try, with a direct click on the element."
  - **First try:** still the plain "It worked."
- **Page summaries:** the mid-word cut happened in the worker, which chopped summaries at exactly 400 characters. `worker/tools.py` now has a `clip()` helper that cuts at the last whole word and adds "…"; the 80-character item labels use it too. The run page also tidies summaries from earlier runs that were already cut mid-word.

**Tested:**
- Types, lint and the production build pass.
- I rendered the run page at phone width against made-up steps, with no console errors:
  - **Retry wording:** steps that worked on the second and third tries showed the new messages.
  - **Old summary:** a 400-character summary that broke off at "…for Sw" now ends "…A login page for…".
- I ran `clip()` on short text, long text and one long word without spaces, and it returned the expected results.

Nothing is committed. Your dev server on port 3000 is still running; I only stopped the test servers I had started.

"""Tests for the egress guard.

Usage: python -m unittest test_egress -v

The redirect test opens a real Chrome window and goes through first_visit, but
stops before the first model call, so it costs nothing. It needs
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in worker/.env only because Stagehand.create requires one.
Test servers listen on loopback, so 127.0.0.1 is treated as public for the
test origin; the redirect target 127.0.0.2 stays private.
"""

import asyncio
import ipaddress
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv(Path(__file__).parent / ".env")

import egress  # noqa: E402

REAL_IS_BLOCKED = egress.is_blocked_address
TEST_ORIGIN = ipaddress.ip_address("127.0.0.1")


def origin_is_public(address):
    return False if address == TEST_ORIGIN else REAL_IS_BLOCKED(address)


class Server:
    """A tiny HTTP server that counts requests and answers with a fixed response."""

    def __init__(self, host: str, response: bytes):
        self.host, self.response, self.hits, self.port = host, response, 0, 0

    async def __aenter__(self):
        async def handle(reader, writer):
            await reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")
            self.hits += 1
            writer.write(self.response)
            await writer.drain()
            writer.close()

        self.server = await asyncio.start_server(handle, self.host, 0)
        self.port = self.server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
        self.server.close()
        await self.server.wait_closed()


def http_response(status: str, headers: str = "", body: str = "") -> bytes:
    return (f"HTTP/1.1 {status}\r\n{headers}Content-Length: {len(body)}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{body}").encode()


async def proxy_request(guard: egress.EgressGuard, request: str) -> str:
    reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", guard.port)
    writer.write(request.encode())
    await writer.drain()
    status = (await reader.readline()).decode().strip()
    writer.close()
    return status


class AddressRules(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_non_public_addresses_are_blocked(self):
        for address in ["127.0.0.1", "10.0.0.5", "172.16.3.4", "192.168.1.1", "169.254.169.254", "100.64.0.1",
                        "0.0.0.0", "::1", "fd00::1", "fe80::1", "::ffff:127.0.0.1", "64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe"]:
            with self.subTest(address=address):
                self.assertTrue(egress.is_blocked_address(ipaddress.ip_address(address)))

    def test_public_addresses_are_allowed(self):
        for address in ["8.8.8.8", "93.184.215.14", "2606:4700:4700::1111"]:
            with self.subTest(address=address):
                self.assertFalse(egress.is_blocked_address(ipaddress.ip_address(address)))


class ProxyRefusals(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_private_targets_are_refused_and_never_contacted(self):
        async with Server("127.0.0.2", http_response("200 OK", body="secret")) as secret:
            guard = egress.EgressGuard()
            await guard.start()
            try:
                plain = await proxy_request(
                    guard, f"GET http://127.0.0.2:{secret.port}/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.2\r\n\r\n")
                tunnel = await proxy_request(guard, "CONNECT localhost:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost:443\r\n\r\n")
                metadata = await proxy_request(
                    guard, "GET http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 169.254.169.254\r\n\r\n")
            finally:
                await guard.close()
        self.assertIn("403", plain)
        self.assertIn("403", tunnel)
        self.assertIn("403", metadata)
        self.assertEqual(secret.hits, 0)
        self.assertEqual([b["host"] for b in guard.blocks], ["127.0.0.2", "localhost", "169.254.169.254"])

    async def test_devtools_port_only_opens_for_an_extension(self):
        async with Server("127.0.0.1", http_response("101 Switching Protocols")) as devtools:
            guard = egress.EgressGuard(devtools_port=devtools.port)
            await guard.start()
            try:
                statuses = {}
                for origin in ("https://evil.example", "chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop"):
                    reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", guard.port)
                    writer.write(f"CONNECT 127.0.0.1:{devtools.port} HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n".encode())
                    await reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")  # the proxy's 200 for the tunnel
                    writer.write(f"GET /devtools/browser/x HTTP/1.1\r\nOrigin: {origin}\r\n"
                                 "Upgrade: websocket\r\n\r\n".encode())
                    await writer.drain()
                    statuses[origin] = (await reader.readline()).decode().strip()
                    writer.close()
            finally:
                await guard.close()
        self.assertEqual(statuses["https://evil.example"], "", "a page must not reach DevTools")
        self.assertIn("101", statuses["chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop"])
        self.assertEqual(devtools.hits, 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(guard.blocks), 1)

    async def test_unresolvable_host_is_not_a_safety_block(self):
        guard = egress.EgressGuard()
        await guard.start()
        try:
            status = await proxy_request(
                guard, "GET http://no-such-host.invalid/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: no-such-host.invalid\r\n\r\n")
        finally:
            await guard.close()
        self.assertIn("502", status)
        self.assertEqual(guard.blocks, [])


class RedirectInRealBrowser(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_redirect_to_private_address_is_refused_and_ends_run_as_blocked(self):
        from visit import first_visit

        async with Server("127.0.0.2", http_response("200 OK", body="secret")) as secret:
            redirect = http_response("302 Found", f"Location: http://127.0.0.2:{secret.port}/secret\r\n")
            async with Server("127.0.0.1", redirect) as origin:
                with mock.patch("egress.is_blocked_address", origin_is_public):
                    result = await first_visit(
                        f"http://127.0.0.1:{origin.port}/", "Look around.", "test-egress-redirect")

        self.assertGreaterEqual(origin.hits, 1, "the allowed origin should have been reached through the proxy")
        self.assertEqual(secret.hits, 0, "the private redirect target must never be contacted")
        self.assertEqual(result["outcome"], "blocked")
        self.assertIn("127.0.0.2", result["reason"])
        self.assertEqual(result["steps"], 0, "the run should end before any model call")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Supabase Postgres Best Practices

Comprehensive performance optimization guide for Postgres, maintained by Supabase. Contains rules across 8 categories, prioritized by impact to guide automated query optimization and schema design.

## When to Apply

Reference these guidelines when:
- Writing SQL queries or designing schemas
- Implementing indexes or query optimization
- Reviewing database performance issues
- Configuring connection pooling or scaling
- Optimizing for Postgres-specific features
- Working with Row-Level Security (RLS)

## Rule Categories by Priority

| Priority | Category | Impact | Prefix |
|----------|----------|--------|--------|
| 1 | Query Performance | CRITICAL | `query-` |
| 2 | Connection Management | CRITICAL | `conn-` |
| 3 | Security & RLS | CRITICAL | `security-` |
| 4 | Schema Design | HIGH | `schema-` |
| 5 | Concurrency & Locking | MEDIUM-HIGH | `lock-` |
| 6 | Data Access Patterns | MEDIUM | `data-` |
| 7 | Monitoring & Diagnostics | LOW-MEDIUM | `monitor-` |
| 8 | Advanced Features | LOW | `advanced-` |

## How to Use

Read individual rule files for detailed explanations and SQL examples:

```
references/query-missing-indexes.md
references/query-partial-indexes.md
references/_sections.md
```

Each rule file contains:
- Brief explanation of why it matters
- Incorrect SQL example with explanation
- Correct SQL example with explanation
- Optional EXPLAIN output or metrics
- Additional context and references
- Supabase-specific notes (when applicable)

- https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/

- https://wiki.postgresql.org/wiki/Performance_Optimization
